gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: We had great ___ at the beach party.
gaps.explanation: 'Fun' is an uncountable noun meaning enjoyment; 'funny' is an adjective meaning causing laughter.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
gaps.hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
gaps.explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.

gaps.sentence: Could I ___ your pen for a moment?
gaps.hint: meaning: take and return later (from someone's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Borrow' means to take something temporarily; 'lend' means to give something temporarily to someone else.

gaps.sentence: The new tax law will ___ every small business in the region.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb (to influence); 'effect' is normally the noun.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
